clauses.reason: Terminated by statutory repeal on 1935-06-14. EO 6417 (November 8, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) adopts the report, recommendations and findings of the Administrator and orders 'that the said supplement be and it is hereby approved': a Supplement to the Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry covering Fair Trade Practices for the Funeral Vehicle and Ambulance subdivision. The order states no period, condition or date of its own, so it has no own-terms end. Its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I: under 3(b) the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, a violation in or affecting interstate commerce was an unfair method of competition, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 (49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, approved June 14, 1935) provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed' and states no later effective date, so the approval's prospective operative effect ended when the resolution was approved. Actor: the Congress by Senate Joint Resolution 113. The date is the resolution's approval date, not a general rule's default: the repeal reaches this command because the command had legal effect only through the repealed provisions. June 16, 1935 is not an end (section 1 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936). Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization recorded in source_notes, not an end date.

Text and identity: EO 6417 is read in full in the registered American Presidency Project (APP) transcription jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6417-supplement-code-fair-competition-for-the-automobile-manufacturing.txt (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-29: the row with the same sha256 (2bdf86c8a311...) in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl is a common-crawl capture (CC-MAIN-2025-26, captured 2025-06-23T22:19:37Z, WARC location recorded so the page can be re-fetched) whose heading is 'Executive Order 6417—Supplement to Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry Covering Fair Trade Practices for the Funeral Vehicle and Ambulance Subdivision' and whose date is 1933-11-08; that date agrees with the date line of the held text ('November 8, 1933.'), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held file is the whole order (recital, operative paragraph, signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line); it carries no order number, so the number comes from the page record. Clauses and sources are quoted from this registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record, the census register ('Executive Order 6417—Supplement to Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry Covering Fair Trade Practices for the Funeral Vehicle and Ambulance Subdivision', 1933-11-08) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (printed page 549: 'Supplement to the Code of Fair Competition for the Auto mobile Manufacturing Industry, covering fair trade practices for the funeral vehicle and ambulance subdivision approved. II NRA Codes 671.'). The WPA list adds the citation II NRA Codes 671. EO 6417 (November 8, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) adopts the report, recommendations and findings of the Administrator and orders 'that the said supplement be and it is hereby approved': a Supplement to the Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry covering Fair Trade Practices for the Funeral Vehicle and Ambulance subdivision. Legal reading: a section 3(a) approval of a code of fair competition with no period, condition or exception of its own; its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I and ended with the repeal of the approval and enforcement provisions on 1935-06-14 (Senate Joint Resolution 113, section 2), unless an earlier end appears. No earlier end was found (see the earlier-end check). 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No own-terms end: the order states no period, condition, 'until' date, 'pending' clause or provisional approval; its only operative command is the approval. The code the supplement supplements, the Automobile Manufacturing Industry code (EO 6258-A of August 26, 1933), has a fixed 'expiration date' term in Article I that later orders extended each time before it arrived: EO 6513-K (December 18, 1933) moved December 31, 1933 to September 4, 1934; EO 6837 (August 31, 1934) moved September 4, 1934 to November 5, 1934; EO 6895 (November 2, 1934), which recites the prior date as November 3, 1934 (a discrepancy with EO 6837's November 5), moved it to February 1, 1935; EO 6955 (January 31, 1935) moved it to June 16, 1935. Every extension issued before the date it replaced, so no stated expiry of the parent code fell before June 14, 1935, and none of these orders cancels, suspends or names the supplement. Searches made on 2026-10-29: (1) a full-text search of every held order text numbered 6200 through 7100 under jobs/*/output/texts (APP, HathiTrust GPO, Wikisource and Federal Register texts; clause-drafts copies excluded) for the code's name; (2) a citation search of the same texts for this order's number; (3) a search of the same texts for general NRA orders that could suspend, cancel or supersede codes: the held general orders (EO 6354 as amended by EO 6710, EO 6646, 6711, 6750-C, 6764 and 6829) prescribe rules, contract terms and delegations, and none suspends, cancels or supersedes the code named here; (4) the census register titles (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) and the WPA 1944 numbered list, read for this code's name; they show no cancellation, suspension or superseding code. Orders for which no text is held (for example EO 6454) could not be searched, so the search covers held texts only. No held record shows this code cancelled or modified under section 10(b), superseded by another code, revoked or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end: it was Title I's original two-year expiry under section 2(c), which section 1 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 replaced with April 1, 1936. The approved code's own text is not held (it is printed in the NRA Codes volumes the WPA list cites), so a code-internal expiry or effective-date term could not be read; no held order records one for this code. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, May 27, 1935) is recorded in source_notes as a validity characterization, not as an end date: it reversed one conviction and held the Live Poultry Code provisions invalid, it did not cancel or withdraw this approving order, and no held record shows this code cancelled or suspended on that date.","independent_command_check":"The order contains one command, the approval. It appoints no one, creates no body, delegates nothing under another statute and directs no agency. It is an approval of a supplement, not an agreement or a licence, and it adds no appointment or direction.","savings_check":"Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. This order states no savings or continuing clause of its own.","scope_check":"The inventory is one clause, the operative paragraph beginning 'Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt' that adopts the Administrator's report and approves the code; the machine inventory is correct and is confirmed. The recital before it states the statutory findings on which the approval rests; the signature, the 'Approval recommended' line and the date line command nothing. The supplement's own text is not held (only this approving order), so any expiry term inside the supplement could not be read. The approval is a single act of one scope; no partial event reaching only part of it was found."}

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. This order states no savings or continuing clause of its own.
